title: Act V, Scene VII

teacherSummary.text: Macbeth, 'tied to a stake' like a baited bear, still fears no man born of woman. He kills Young Siward in single combat and scorns swords 'brandish'd by man that's of a woman born.' Macduff enters seeking only Macbeth, refusing to strike at hired kerns. Siward tells Malcolm the castle is 'gently render'd' and that some of the tyrant's men fight on their side.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Thou wast born of woman” slowly and put it in my own words: After killing Young Siward in single combat, Macbeth says the boy was born of woman. Next, craft. I notice he speaks as if the prophecy makes him invulnerable, mocking the dead young man. The strongest word is “woman”: it recalls the witches' promise that no man born of a woman could harm him. Then, effect. Why is Macbeth so confident after killing Young Siward? My answer: Macbeth believes the prophecy protects him; his confidence is about to collapse when he meets Macduff, which shows how the witches' riddles have trapped him.
